_comment: Byte patches the launcher applies to the base client to produce the runnable
one. Every entry is LENGTH-PRESERVING and EXPECT-CHECKED: the launcher writes
nothing unless the bytes already there are exactly what 'expect' says, which is
what makes a build-locked patch safe to apply on a player's machine.
Offsets are FILE offsets into the base, not virtual addresses. 'va' is recorded
for cross-referencing a disassembler only; nothing reads it.
See Extract-ClientPatches.py for why base and patch list are split the way they
are, and Build-ClientPatch.py for how this becomes a manifest block.
The PE checksum is NOT listed here. Build-ClientPatch.py computes it over the
finished file and appends it as a final entry, so that every scrap of PE
knowledge stays in the toolchain and the launcher only ever copies, pokes and

patches.note: Drops IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE from .zdata (0xE0000040 -> 0xC0000040). .zdata is a 4 KB zero-filled RWX page at a fixed address (0xDD1000; relocs are stripped and there is no ASLR), which is the landing pad the known 3.3.5a client RCE writes shellcode into. NX_COMPAT is set, so clearing the bit makes exploitation a crash instead. Verified unreferenced: a whole-file scan for absolute pointers into 0xDD1000-0xDD2000 found only misaligned false positives inside instruction encodings, and our own caves are in .text. Equivalent to stoneharry/RCEPatcher, which pokes the same byte.
Mouse-cam 1/4. Border-clamp helper written into a dead int3 run. Part of the windowed-mode mouselook fix shipped 2026-08-28.

Mouse-cam 2/4. Replaces the broken mouselook recenter, which computed the window centre from GetWindowRect().right/2 and .bottom/2 - screen coordinates, and right/2 rather than (left+right)/2, so the centre was wrong whenever the window was not at the screen origin. Drops recentering entirely and nudges the tracked cursor 1px per call off a 50px border.
Mouse-cam 3/4. At the compare site, jumps out to the ScreenToClient thunk so the polled cursor is compared in client space against the real tracked pair, rather than against the bogus centre pair.
Mouse-cam 4/4. The ScreenToClient thunk itself, in a second dead int3 run. Reuses the existing USER32 import; adds none.
